subject: business-studies
title: Hard vs Soft HRM and Recruitment
welcome_lead: Treat staff as a cost or an asset - and pick the right hire either way.
meta_desc: A-Level HR: hard vs soft HRM, recruitment, selection, training.
final_note: Hard HRM cuts cost short term; soft HRM builds capability long term.

concepts.def: Treats staff as a resource to be minimised in cost.
Treats staff as a valuable long-term asset.
Attracting candidates to apply for vacancies.
Choosing the best candidate from applicants.
Training away from the normal workstation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hard HRM uses zero-hours contracts, monitors output and minimises pay. Soft HRM invests in training, security and engagement - turnover is lower and innovation higher.
Internal recruitment is cheaper and motivating but limits new thinking. External recruitment brings fresh skills but costs more and risks longer induction.
On-the-job training is cheap and relevant but the trainer's bad habits transfer. Off-the-job training is structured and brings best practice but loses production hours.

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Economies of scale means a business saves the economy money.
Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
